title: Segments, Midpoints and Partitioning a Segment
seo_title: Geometry Segments, Midpoints and Partitions Worksheets (TEKS G.2A)
standard_text: G.2A determine the coordinates of a point that is a given fractional distance less than one from one end of a line segment to the other in one- and two-dimensional coordinate systems, including finding the midpoint
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.2A: segment addition, midpoints, and finding a point a fraction of the way along a segment on a number line and the coordinate plane. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A ratio 1 : 2 means 1/3 of the way.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Segment addition: if B is between A and C, then AB + BC = AC.
  • Midpoint: ((x1 + x2) ÷ 2, (y1 + y2) ÷ 2).
  • A point k of the way from A to B is A + k(B − A). Do it for x and for y.
  • A ratio m : n means the fraction m ÷ (m + n) of the way.

Examples

Example

A(−2, 1), B(10, 7); P is 1/3 of the way from A to B

B − A = (12, 6)

1/3 of it = (4, 2)

Answer: P(2, 3)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Measuring from the wrong endpointStart at A when it says “from A”.
Using m : n as m/n1 : 2 means 1/3 of the way.
Adding the fraction of the length to the wrong coordinateWork with x and y separately.

faq.a: Determine the coordinates of a point that is a given fractional distance less than one from one end of a line segment to the other in one- and two-dimensional coordinate systems, including finding the midpoint.

faq.q: Is the midpoint 1/2 of the way?

faq.a: The point is 2/5 of the way from the first endpoint.
Yes, but these worksheets use whole numbers.

items.q: A = (−6, 4) and B = (−6, 14). Point P is 35 of the way from A to B. What are the coordinates of P?
items.e: P = A + 35(B − A) = (−6, 4) + 35(0, 10) = (−6, 10).
